page.overview:
Who is Delilah?

is the protagonist of 1:35 A.M., the first story in the book of the same name. She later briefly appears in the tenth Stitchwraith Stinger. Delilah is a young woman who becomes extremely exhausted and pessimistic after her divorce. One day, she purchases an electronic doll in hopes that it's alarm clock aid against her exhaustion, but is instead haunted by it.

Delilah has wavy shoulder-length dark hair and dark eyes. She used to wear makeup, but after her divorce she decides to keep her face bare. Even without makeup, Delilah is pretty, with a modeling agency having told her that she's a large chin away from having classically beautiful features.

Delilah is said to have an “obsessive personality,” meaning she’ll latch onto a perspective and have difficulty letting go. Following her divorce, she takes on a negative outlook on life and becomes stuck in a state of perpetual exhaustion. Delilah also seems to suffer from brain fog and depersonalization, making it hard to think clearly and stay in sync with her senses. She loves sleep but is unable to get enough due to her work schedule, and her low energy makes her quick to frustration. Delilah is entertained by looking through garage sales, wanting to know what people used, collected, loved, and don’t want around anymore. It was theorized by her therapist that this gives her a glimpse into family life, reminding her what “normal” looks like. Unlike her friend Harper, Delilah tries to have grounded beliefs, even refusing to believe her experiences with Ella were supernatural.

Delilah entered the foster care system after her parents both died when she was eleven. She bounced from home to home, finally landing in a house with a couple where the husband was a former military man who imposed strict rules on those living there. The other foster kid there was Harper, and the girls became friends in their less-than-ideal situation.
